match.reason: No bank point teaches the distinction between GPs, allied health (such as physiotherapists and psychologists) and alternative health (such as naturopathy); the closest point, community health resources, only covers GPs in passing and focuses on access barriers, so it is a related idea rather than the same one.

draft.title: GPs, allied and alternative health
card: GP
a general practitioner, a doctor who treats common problems and checks overall health. A GP is usually the first stop and can refer a patient to a specialist or another health professional.
Allied health
university-trained professionals who each work in one area of care, such as physiotherapists, psychologists and dietitians. They are regulated and use treatments backed by scientific evidence.
Alternative health
practices outside conventional medicine, such as naturopathy and homeopathy. Their treatments often have limited scientific evidence of working.
People may use these services together. For example, a GP may suggest a physiotherapist for an injury, while a person may choose to see a naturopath on their own.
draft.remember: GPs are usually the first stop, allied health adds focused care, and alternative health sits outside conventional medicine.

a.q: Which health professional is an example of allied health?
opts: A psychologist
A naturopath
A general practitioner
A homeopath
a.why: A psychologist is trained in one area of care, mental health, and uses evidence-based methods, so is allied health. A naturopath is the most tempting wrong answer, but naturopathy is an alternative health practice outside conventional medicine.
a.clue: Look for a university-trained professional who works in one area of care.

b.q: Ravi hurts his knee playing netball in Geelong. He books a visit with his local doctor, who sends him to a physiotherapist. Which describes these two services?
opts: A GP as first stop, then allied health
Allied health first, then a GP referral
Alternative health first, then a GP referral
A GP as first stop, then alternative health
b.why: The doctor is a GP, who is usually the first stop and can refer a patient on. A physiotherapist works in one area of care and uses evidence-based treatment, so is allied health, not alternative health.
b.clue: Name each person's role, then check the order Ravi saw them.

b.best: A GP as first stop, then allied health

problems.detail: The card says allied health professionals 'are regulated', right after listing dietitians. In Australia, dietitians (and some other allied health groups, such as speech pathologists) are not registered under AHPRA; they are self-regulated through professional bodies. A safer wording is 'many are registered with AHPRA' or 'most are regulated'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and each has one clear right answer. One small fact issue: the card says allied health professionals are all regulated, but dietitians are not nationally registered in Australia, so the wording should be softened.
